name: Portumna bridge
facts: Designed by London engineer C. E. Stanier, Portumna Bridge was completed in 1911, featuring steel girders atop concrete‑filled cast‑iron cylinders that exemplify early 20th‑century bridge engineering.
The bridge’s central span rests on Hayes’s Island, which splits the Shannon into two channels and once housed a bridge‑operator’s house predating the current structure.

In October 2008, the original opening section was replaced, while the swing bridge over the navigation channel remains operational, opening only at fixed times for vessels exceeding four feet of air draft.
